notes.title: TechFlow Advisory Notes — Product-Market Fit
notes.content:
TechFlow Product-Market Fit Observations (Updated Feb 2026)

Strengths:
- AI agent orchestration is genuinely novel — no direct competitor matches the memory system
- Developer experience is excellent, leading to organic growth via word-of-mouth
- Team velocity is impressive for 12 people

Suggestions shared with Alex & Sarah:
1. Enterprise pivot considerations — SOC2 and HIPAA compliance would unlock enterprise contracts
2. Consider a developer evangelism hire (before VP Sales)
3. Usage-based pricing may work better than per-seat for their power-user segment
4. Community building — open source some non-core modules to build developer ecosystem

Overall assessment: Strong product, needs commercial acceleration. Alex is the secret weapon — his technical instincts are top-tier.

notes.title: Startup Ecosystem Notes — SF Bay Area Q1 2026
notes.content:
Bay Area Startup Ecosystem — Q1 2026 Observations

Funding environment:
- Seed rounds normalizing at $3-5M (down from $5-8M peak in 2021)
- Series A bar is high: need $1M+ ARR or exceptional growth
- AI companies still getting premium valuations (2-3x vs non-AI)
- Later stage (B/C) very selective — unit economics matter again

Trends I'm seeing:
- AI agent companies everywhere — maybe 50% of my deal flow is agent-related
- Developer tools renaissance (inspired by Cursor, Replit success)
- Climate tech gaining traction with corporate buyers
- Healthcare AI finally seeing real adoption (post-COVID regulatory easing)

Concerns:
- AI agent bubble forming — too many companies, not enough differentiation
- Talent wars for ML engineers (median comp: $400K+ total for senior)
- Office market still depressed — many startups permanently remote

My investment focus for 2026:
- AI infrastructure (picks & shovels)
- Vertical SaaS with AI core
- Avoid: horizontal chatbots, me-too agent platforms

notes.title: Industry Trend Analysis — Enterprise AI Adoption
notes.content:
Enterprise AI Adoption Trends — 2026

Key findings from industry research:

1. Adoption rates:
   - 78% of Fortune 500 have AI initiatives (up from 55% in 2024)
   - Average enterprise AI budget: $5-15M/year
   - Most common use cases: customer support (45%), code generation (38%), document processing (35%)

2. Buyer behavior:
   - Security/compliance now #1 purchase criteria (above price)
   - Preference for platform solutions over point solutions
   - Average sales cycle: 6-9 months for $100K+ deals
   - Champion: typically VP Engineering or CTO

3. Pricing:
   - Per-seat dying — usage-based gaining share
   - Enterprise average contract: $120K/year
   - SMB average: $15K/year
   - Freemium still works for developer tools (5% conversion)

4. Competitive dynamics:
   - Microsoft Copilot is the 800-lb gorilla
   - Google and Salesforce close behind
   - Startups winning on specialization and speed
   - Open source (LangChain, LlamaIndex) setting the floor

notes.title: Pitch Evaluation Framework
notes.content:
Victor's Angel Investment Framework

Scoring (1-10 on each, minimum 35/50 to invest):

1. Team (weight: 30%)
   - Technical depth
   - Domain expertise
   - Founder chemistry
   - Hustle/grit signals

2. Market (weight: 25%)
   - TAM > $10B
   - Growing > 20%/year
   - Timing (not too early/late)
   - Regulatory tailwinds

3. Product (weight: 20%)
   - Clear differentiation
   - Technical moat
   - Demo quality
   - User feedback

4. Traction (weight: 15%)
   - Revenue or strong usage
   - Growth rate
   - Retention/engagement
   - Customer quality

5. Deal (weight: 10%)
   - Valuation reasonableness
   - Terms
   - Co-investors
   - Pro-rata rights

Recent example: TechFlow scored 42/50 (Team:9, Market:8, Product:9, Traction:7, Deal:9)
